$comment: Settings of pipeline:river-lines (WP 5.1): each approved river's course assembled from the display lines (APRHI inside the province, IGN outside; precedence APRHI > IGN > HydroRIVERS, owner). Values set from the WP 5.0a/5.0b measurements (2026-10-13): line endpoints of different lines either meet within 1 m (22.6% of endpoints) or lie 50 m or more apart (only 2.4% fall between 1 and 50 m), so snapM 50 joins clean junctions without merging separate lines; the own lines of one river can stop short of each other: R. Quinto (Popopis) lines meet within 0-600 m (WP 5.0a), so extensionGapM is 600; a line that leaves another mid-piece is covered by attachM instead. snapM: line endpoints within this distance (m) are one junction (the graph node). corridorM: candidate pieces are limited to the river's own root(s) (a river's course never leaves them); within them, the drawn pieces within this distance (m) of the river's HydroRIVERS reaches (South America Albers), plus every piece that carries the river's own name wherever it lies; the anchors must also lie within it of the reaches. gapSearchM: a virtual gap edge may join two dangling line ends (a node with one piece, or one touching another river's course) of different connected pieces up to this far apart (m); gaps on a course are recorded in gaps.json and never filled. gapNeighbours: each dangling end gets virtual edges to at most this many nearest ends of other components (bounds the graph; added by the builder, not in the brief). Besides those, every pair of components within gapSearchM is joined once between their closest nodes (any node, loops included), so a path exists whenever the lines are chained within gapSearchM. weights: cost per metre of a piece on the cheapest source-to-mouth path: own = a piece named as the river (name or alias, a parenthesised alias in the piece name is ignored), unnamed = a piece with no name (APRHI starred names count as unnamed), other = a piece named otherwise; gap = per metre of straight virtual edge. A path prefers own pieces, bridges over unnamed ones, and uses another river's name only when nothing else connects. excludeClasses: piece classes (APRHI Clase or IGN class, case and accent insensitive) never used on a course, for channels that carry no water: APRHI TIPO 'Paleocauce' (relict channel, 20 lines, 78.6 km). Neither APRHI nor IGN has a canal class; APRHI SISTEMATIZ 'SI' is not used because it includes main rivers (R. Quinto 115.9 km, R. Jesús María 150 km); the meaning of both values is unverified until APRHI's metadata is read (PENDING.md). mouthLakeIds: lakes (lakes.parquet ids) a course that ends at them is extended to: from the mouth it follows own-named pieces to the one with an endpoint closest to the lake ('aprhi-nat-1582' is Mar Chiquita; the own lines of Primero, Jesús María and Dulce end 0-0.44 km from it, measured in WP 5.0b). lakeTouchM: an endpoint within this distance (m) of a mouth lake touches it. anchorMaxM: the source and mouth anchors (where the course starts and ends) take the nearest line junction that touches a piece named as the river, within this distance (m) of the upstream end of the most upstream HydroRIVERS reach / the downstream end of the mouth reach; failing that, the nearest junction with a real piece. The report says which rule chose each anchor and checks both anchors are within this distance (the 15″ paths can end kilometres from the mapped channel). extensionGapM: the own-named extensions (mouth to a lake's shore, source up the river) may cross a break of up to this length (m) between the ends of two own-named lines that no chain of own-named pieces joins (beyond snapM); each break is recorded as a gap of kind 'extension' in gaps.json. A mouth extension still has to reach within lakeTouchM of a mouthLakeIds lake. When the mouth anchor itself cannot reach the lake, the extension may start from another node of the course, which then ends the course there. After the course and the claims, every unclaimed own-named piece joined to the course through own-named pieces only is added as an 'arm' (owner, 2026-10-13: tramos that follow the river's channel are part of the river); arms are not counted in the course km. attachM: a line end within this distance (m) of the interior of another piece attaches to it there, without splitting the piece (course.parquet keeps whole pieces; the attachment only adds connectivity). Own-named line ends attach to this river's course: as an arm, or, for the mouth extension, as the continuation (the course then ends at the attached piece's downstream end). A line end that attaches to the interior of a piece an earlier river holds ends the river's course there (a confluence). Every attachment is recorded in gaps.json (kind 'attach', with the distance). Evidence: R. Jesús María's lower arm aprhi:826:2#0 starts 100.5 m from the interior of its main line's piece aprhi:826:0#20 (5 km long), 1,327.5 m from the nearest piece end; attachM 500 is the same distance as the confluence search used for other rivers. Rivers are processed receivers first (the river a mouth flows into is processed before the rivers that flow into it), so a tributary finds the receiver's pieces already held. ownShareTarget: a check that only warns until the settings are calibrated; a river's course should hold at least this share of the own-named km among its candidates.
